evals.name: nats-jetstream-acks-terms-introduced-and-claims-grounded
evals.prompt: Explain how NATS JetStream consumer acknowledgment works and what happens when acks are late or missing.
evals.expected_output: Every technical term outside a senior backend developer's general baseline (e.g. ack floor, AckExplicit/AckAll/AckNone, ack wait, redelivery, MaxDeliver, WorkQueue semantics) gets a brief definition or lead-in sentence at its first use — no bare jargon drops mid-explanation. Abstract claims about delivery guarantees or failure behavior are anchored by a concrete example, config/code snippet, or verifiable fact rather than left as unanchored generalities; specifics the model cannot verify are marked as such instead of asserted.

evals.name: dotnet-channel-backpressure-terms-introduced-and-claims-grounded
evals.prompt: Explain backpressure in .NET Channel<T> and when bounded vs unbounded channels matter.
evals.expected_output: Every domain-specific term (e.g. backpressure, bounded/unbounded channel, BoundedChannelFullMode, WriteAsync suspension, rendezvous) is introduced with a short definition or contextual lead-in at first use. Abstract claims (e.g. about memory growth, producer/consumer speed mismatch, when bounding matters) are each paired with a code snippet or concrete worked example; the answer does not pad with definitions of things a senior .NET developer already knows (variables, async/await basics).
